87.subject: Botany
87.text: Biosphere reserves differ from National Parks and Wildlife sanctuaries because in the former
options: human beings are not allowed to enter
people are an integral part of the system
plants are paid greater attention than the animals
living organisms are brought from all over the world and preserved for posterity.
87.sol:
Biosphere reserves, National Park and wild life sanctuaries are all protected areas but differ from each other in some ways.
National parks are reserved for betterment of wild life. Cultivation, grazing forestry and habitat manipulations are not allowed.
Sanctuaries are tracts of land with or with out lake where wild life can take refuge without being hunted. Harvesting of timber, collection of forest products, tilling of land, private ownership of land etc., are allowed. Biosphere reserves are multipurpose protected area which are meant for preserving genetic diversity in representative ecosystems of various national biomass and unique biological communities by protecting wild life, traditional life style of tribals and domesticated plant/animal genetic resources.
Each biosphere reserve has 3 zones - (i) core or natural zone - where no human activity is allowed, (ii) Buffer zone - limited human activity is allowed like education and research (iii) Transition zone - It is the outer most zone where an active cooperation is present between reserve management and local people for activities like agriculture, tourism and forestry.

Lengths of sections A P B$ and A Q B$ are $r \theta$ and $r(2 \pi-\theta)$

& \Rightarrow|z|^2-2 z-2 i \bar{z}+4 i+|z|^2+2 i z-2 \bar{z}-4 i= \\
& \Rightarrow 2|z|^2-2(z+\bar{z})+2 i(z-\bar{z})=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x^2+y^2-2 x-2 y=0 \quad(\because z=x+i y) \\
& \Rightarrow(x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=(\sqrt{2})^2 \\
& \Rightarrow \text{ Required area }=\frac{\pi r^2}{2}=\frac{\pi(\sqrt{2})^2}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}
\end{aligned}$

7475.text: If $1, z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_{n-1}$ are the $n$th roots of unity, $\left(1-z_1\right)   \left(1-z_2\right)$\ldots $\left(1-z_{n-1}\right)$ is equal to

We have given that, $1, z_1, z_2, z_3, \ldots . z_{n-1}$ are the $n$th root of unity.
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad z^n-1=(z-1)\left(z-z_1\right)\left(z-z_2\right), \ldots .,\left(z-z_{n-1}\right) \\
& (z-1)\left(z^{n-1}+z^{n-2}+\ldots . .+z^2+z+1\right) \\
& =(z-1)\left(z-z_1\right)+\ldots . .\left(z-z_{n-1}\right) \\
& \left(z^{n-1}+z^{n-2}+\ldots . .+z^2+z+1\right)=\left(z-z_1\right) \\
& \left(z-z_1\right)=\left(z-z_{n-1}\right)
\end{aligned}$
Put $z=1$, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& (1+1+\ldots .+n \text{ times }) \\
& =\left(1-z_1\right)\left(1-z_2\right)+\ldots .\left(1-z_{n-1}\right) \\
& n=\left(1-z_1\right)\left(1-z_2\right) \ldots\left(1-z_{n-1}\right)
\end{aligned}$

We have a parallelogram $ABCD$,

whose vertices are $A\left(2, 4, - 1\right), B\left(3, 6, - 1\right), C\left(4, 5, 1\right)$

Now, assume the fourth vertex $D\left(x, y, z\right)$

Now, we know that, diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other,

So, coordinate of $E$, as mid-point of $AC$ is $\left(3, \dfrac{9}{2}, 0\right) . . . \left(1\right)$

As mid-point of $BD$ is $\left(\dfrac{x + 3}{2}, \dfrac{y + 6}{2}, \dfrac{z - 1}{2}\right) . . . \left(2\right)$
So, comparing $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right)$, 

$\dfrac{x + 3}{2} = 3 ⇒ x = 3$

$\dfrac{y + 6}{2} = \dfrac{9}{2} ⇒ y = 3$ and 

$\dfrac{z - 1}{2} = 0 ⇒ z = 1$

So, the coordinate of $D$ is $\left(3, 3, 1\right)$.

19362.text: Helium gas goes through a cycle $ABCDA$ (consisting of two isochoric and two isobaric lines) as shown in figure. The efficiency of this cycle is approximately
19362.sol:
Helium is mono atomic gas, for which
${C}_{V} = \dfrac{3}{2}R . {C}_{p} = \dfrac{5}{2}R$

Work done by the gas in one complete cycle $W =$ area $ABCDA = {p}_{0}{V}_{0}$

From $A to B$, Heat given to gas $= n{C}_{V}\Delta T$

$= 1 \times \left(\dfrac{3}{2}R\right) \times \Delta T = \dfrac{3}{2}{V}_{0}\left(\Deltap\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}{V}_{0}{p}_{0}$

From $B$~to $C$,~heat given to gas $= n{C}_{p}\Delta T$

$= 1 \times \left(\dfrac{5}{2}R\right) \times \Delta T = \dfrac{5}{2}\left(2{p}_{0}\right)\Delta V = 5{p}_{0}{V}_{0}$

Efficiency of cycle $= \dfrac{Workdonebythegas / cycle}{Totalheatgiventogas / cycle}$

$= \dfrac{{p}_{0}{V}_{0}}{\dfrac{3}{2}{p}_{0}{V}_{0} + 5{p}_{0}{V}_{0}} = \dfrac{2}{13}$

Efficiency $\left(%\right) = \dfrac{2}{13} \times 100 = 15 . 4 %$

19620.sol:
Toluene reacts with conc. $HNO_{3}$ and $H_{2}SO_{4}$ (nitrating mixture) to undergo electrophilic aromatic substitution. Since the methyl group is ortho/para directing, the major product [B] is p-nitrotoluene.

Reduction of p-nitrotoluene with $Fe/HCl$ converts the nitro group ($-NO_{2}$) into an amino group ($-NH_{2}$), yielding [C], which is p-toluidine (4-methylaniline).

Reaction of p-toluidine with acetic anhydride $(CH_{3}CO)_{2}O$ results in the acetylation of the amino group to form [D], which is 4-methylacetanilide.

Answer: 4-methylacetanilide

19830.text:
Consider the following equilibrium,
$2\text{NO}(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g); K_{C_1} = 2.4 \times 10^{20}\text{NO}(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{Br}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{NOBr}(g); K_{C_2} = 1.4$
Calculate $K_C$ for the reaction,
$\frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{Br}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{NOBr}(g)$
19830.sol:
Target reaction: $\dfrac{1}{2}N_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}O_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}Br_2(g) \rightleftharpoons NOBr(g)$

Reverse reaction 1 and multiply by $\dfrac{1}{2}$:
$\dfrac{1}{2}N_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons NO(g)$, $K'' = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{K_1}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2.4 \times 10^{20}}}$

Add reaction 2 as it is:
$NO(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}Br_2(g) \rightleftharpoons NOBr(g)$, $K_2 = 1.4$

$K_C = K'' \times K_2 = \dfrac{1.4}{\sqrt{2.4 \times 10^{20}}} = \dfrac{1.4}{\sqrt{2.4} \times 10^{10}}$

$= \dfrac{1.4 \times 0.64}{10^{10}} \approx \dfrac{0.896}{10^{10}} = 8.96 \times 10^{-11}$

20963.subject: Mathematics
20963.text: The approximate value of $f(5.001)$, where $f(x)=x^3-7 x^2+10$
20963.sol:
The function is given by $f(x) = x^{3} - 7x^{2} + 10$.

The approximate value of $f(x + \Delta x)$ is given by $f(x) + f'(x) \Delta x$.

Here, $x = 5$ and $\Delta x = 0.001$.

First, calculate $f(5) = (5)^{3} - 7(5)^{2} + 10 = 125 - 7(25) + 10 = 125 - 175 + 10 = -40$.

Next, find the derivative $f'(x) = 3x^{2} - 14x$.

Evaluate $f'(5) = 3(5)^{2} - 14(5) = 3(25) - 70 = 75 - 70 = 5$.

Now, calculate the approximation $f(5.001) \approx f(5) + f'(5) \Delta x = -40 + 5(0.001) = -40 + 0.005 = -39.995$.

Answer: $-39.995$

21127.subject: Mathematics
21127.text: $S \equiv x^2+y^2-2 x-4 y-4=0$ and $S^{\prime} \equiv x^2+y^2-4 x-2 y-16=0$ are two circles the point $(-2,-1)$ lies
21127.sol:
Let the given circles be $S(x, y) = x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 4y - 4 = 0$ and $S'(x, y) = x^2 + y^2 - 4x - 2y - 16 = 0$.

To determine the position of the point $P(-2,-1)$ with respect to circle $S$, substitute the coordinates of $P$ into the expression for $S$:

$S(-2,-1) = (-2)^2 + (-1)^2 - 2(-2) - 4(-1) - 4 = 4 + 1 + 4 + 4 - 4 = 9$.

Since $S(-2,-1) = 9 > 0$, the point $P(-2,-1)$ lies outside the circle $S$.

To determine the position of the point $P(-2,-1)$ with respect to circle $S'$, substitute the coordinates of $P$ into the expression for $S'$:

$S'(-2,-1) = (-2)^2 + (-1)^2 - 4(-2) - 2(-1) - 16 = 4 + 1 + 8 + 2 - 16 = -1$.

Since $S'(-2,-1) = -1 < 0$, the point $P(-2,-1)$ lies inside the circle $S'$.

Therefore, the point lies inside $S'$ only.

Answer: inside $S^{\prime}$ only

21319.subject: Mathematics
21319.text: $The solution of the differential equation \dfrac{d y}{d x}=e^{x+y}+x^2 e^y$ is
21319.sol:
The given differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x+y} + x^2 e^y$.

Factoring out $e^y$ from the right side, we get $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^y(e^x + x^2)$.

Separating the variables, we have $\dfrac{dy}{e^y} = (e^x + x^2) dx$, which can be written as $e^{-y} dy = (e^x + x^2) dx$.

Integrating both sides, we get $\int e^{-y} dy = \int (e^x + x^2) dx$.

Performing the integration, we obtain $-e^{-y} = e^x + \dfrac{x^3}{3} + c$.

Rearranging the terms, we get $e^x + e^{-y} + \dfrac{x^3}{3} = -c$. Since $-c$ is an arbitrary constant, we can write this as $e^x + e^{-y} + \dfrac{x^3}{3} = C$.

Answer: $e^x+e^{-y}+\dfrac{x^3}{3}=c$

21377.subject: Mathematics
21377.sol:
Given $\log y = \log(\sin x) - x^2$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{1}{y} \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cot x - 2x$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y(\cot x - 2x)$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{dy}{dx} \cot x - y \csc^2 x - 2x \dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2y$

The given expression is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 4x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 4x^2y$. Substituting $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ into the expression:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 4x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 4x^2y = \left( \dfrac{dy}{dx} \cot x - y \csc^2 x - 2x \dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2y \right) + 4x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 4x^2y$

$= \dfrac{dy}{dx} \cot x - y \csc^2 x + 2x \dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2y + 4x^2y$

$= \dfrac{dy}{dx} (\cot x + 2x) - y \csc^2 x - 2y + 4x^2y$

Substituting $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y(\cot x - 2x)$:

$= y(\cot x - 2x)(\cot x + 2x) - y \csc^2 x - 2y + 4x^2y$

$= y(\cot^2 x - 4x^2) - y \csc^2 x - 2y + 4x^2y$

$= y \cot^2 x - 4x^2y - y \csc^2 x - 2y + 4x^2y$

$= y(\cot^2 x - \csc^2 x) - 2y$

Using the identity $\csc^2 x - \cot^2 x = 1$, we get $\cot^2 x - \csc^2 x = -1$:

$= y(-1) - 2y = -3y$

Answer: $-3y$

21770.subject: Mathematics
21770.text: If the matrix $A$ is such that $A\left(\begin{array}{cc}-1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1\end{array}\right)=\left(\begin{array}{cc}-4 & 1 \\ 7 & 7\end{array}\right)$ then $A$ is equal to
21770.sol:
Let $A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$. The given equation is $AB = C$, where $C = \begin{pmatrix} -4 & 1 \\ 7 & 7 \end{pmatrix}$.

To find $A$, we compute $A = CB^{-1}$.

First, find the determinant of $B$: $|B| = (-1)(1) - (2)(3) = -1 - 6 = -7$.

The inverse of $B$ is given by $B^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|B|} \text{adj}(B) = \dfrac{1}{-7} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ -3 & -1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -1/7 & 2/7 \\ 3/7 & 1/7 \end{pmatrix}$.

Now, calculate $A = CB^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 & 1 \\ 7 & 7 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} -1/7 & 2/7 \\ 3/7 & 1/7 \end{pmatrix}$.

The first row of $A$ is: $a_{11} = (-4)(-1/7) + (1)(3/7) = 4/7 + 3/7 = 1$ and $a_{12} = (-4)(2/7) + (1)(1/7) = -8/7 + 1/7 = -1$.

The second row of $A$ is: $a_{21} = (7)(-1/7) + (7)(3/7) = -1 + 3 = 2$ and $a_{22} = (7)(2/7) + (7)(1/7) = 2 + 1 = 3$.

Thus, $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$.

Answer: $\left(\begin{array}{cc}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{array}\right)$

22261.text: $The expression \dfrac{2 \tan A}{1-\cot A}+\dfrac{2 \cot A}{1-\tan A}$ can be written as
22261.sol:
$\dfrac{2\tan A}{1 - \cot A} + \dfrac{2\cot A}{1 - \tan A}$

$= 2\left[\dfrac{\frac{\sin A}{\cos A}}{\frac{\sin A - \cos A}{\sin A}} + \dfrac{\frac{\cos A}{\sin A}}{\frac{\cos A - \sin A}{\cos A}}\right]$

$= 2 \left[\dfrac{\sin^2 A}{\cos A(\sin A - \cos A)} + \dfrac{\cos^2 A}{\sin A(\cos A - \sin A)}\right]

$= 2 $\left[\dfrac{\sin^2 A}{\cos A(\sin A - \cos A)} - \dfrac{\cos^2 A}{\sin A(\sin A - \cos A)}\right]$

$= 2 \left[\dfrac{\sin^3 A - \cos^3 A}{\sin A \cos A(\sin A - \cos A)}\right]

23260.subject: Physics
23260.text: Fusion reaction is more energetic than fission reaction because
options: In the fusion reaction lighter nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus
Uncontrolled chain reaction is taking place In the fusion reaction.
The energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fusion reaction is larger than the energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fission reaction.
Fusion reaction is taking place at very high temperature
23260.sol:
The energy released in a nuclear reaction is determined by the mass defect, which is the difference between the mass of the reactants and the mass of the products. This mass defect is converted into energy according to Einstein's mass-energy equivalence relation, $E = \Delta m c^2$.

In fission, a heavy nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei, whereas in fusion, two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus. The binding energy per nucleon curve shows that the binding energy per nucleon increases significantly when light nuclei fuse to form a medium-mass nucleus, compared to the change when a heavy nucleus undergoes fission.

Consequently, the energy released per unit mass of the fuel (the mass defect per unit mass of the reactants) is significantly higher for fusion reactions than for fission reactions. This makes fusion reactions more energetic per unit mass of the fuel involved.

Answer: The energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fusion reaction is larger than the energy released per unit mass of the fuel in fission reaction.

23665.subject: Physics
23665.text: In Young's double slit interference experiment, using two coherent waves of different amplitudes, the intensities ratio between bright and dark fringes is 3. Then, the value of the ratio of the amplitudes of the wave that arrive there is
23665.sol:
Let the amplitudes of the two coherent waves be $A_1 and A_2$. The intensity of a wave is proportional to the square of its amplitude, $I \propto A^2$.

The maximum intensity $I_{max}$ at bright fringes is given by $I_{max} = (A_1 + A_2)^2$ and the minimum intensity $I_{min}$ at dark fringes is given by $I_{min} = (A_1 - A_2)^2$.

Given the ratio of intensities is $\dfrac{I_{max}}{I_{min}} = 3$, we have $\dfrac{(A_1 + A_2)^2}{(A_1 - A_2)^2} = 3$.

Taking the square root on both sides, we get $\dfrac{A_1 + A_2}{A_1 - A_2} = \sqrt{3}$.

Applying componendo and dividendo, $\dfrac{(A_1 + A_2) + (A_1 - A_2)}{(A_1 + A_2) - (A_1 - A_2)} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$.

Simplifying the expression, $\dfrac{2A_1}{2A_2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$, which gives the ratio of amplitudes $\dfrac{A_1}{A_2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$.

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}-1}\right)$

23768.subject: Physics
23768.text: A motor cyclist starts from the top of an inclined plane of height h to go around a globe of death trap of radius r. The ratio of minimum height 'h' of the inclined plane to the radius 'r' of the death globe in order to go around the death globe successfully is
23768.sol:
By conservation of mechanical energy, the velocity of the motorcyclist at the bottom of the inclined plane is given by

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$

$v = \sqrt{2gh}$

To successfully complete the vertical circular loop (globe of death) of radius $r$, the minimum velocity required at the lowest point is

$v \ge \sqrt{5gr}$

For the minimum height $h$, we equate the velocities:

$\sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{5gr}$

$2gh = 5gr$

$\dfrac{h}{r} = \dfrac{5}{2}$

The ratio of the minimum height to the radius is $5:2$.

Answer: $5:2$

25616.subject: Mathematics
25616.text:
Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the set of all real numbers and let $i = \sqrt{-1}$. Consider the matrices
$S = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ and $T = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.
Let $a, b, c, d$ be real numbers such that
$ST = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$.
Let
$H = \{x + iy : x, y \in \mathbb{R} \text{ and } y > 0\}$.
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
options: If $m$ is an integer greater than $2$ such that $(ST)^2 = (ST)^m$, then $m$ is an integer multiple of $8$
If $z \in H$, then $\dfrac{az + b}{cz + d} \in H$
25616.sol:
We are given the matrices $S = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ and $T = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

First, we compute the product $ST$:
$ST = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

Comparing this with $ST = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$, we get $a = 0$, $b = -1$, $c = 1$, and $d = 1$.

Evaluating Option (A):
$\dfrac{b + ia}{d + ic} = \dfrac{-1 + i(0)}{1 + i(1)} = \dfrac{-1}{1 + i} = \dfrac{-1(1 - i)}{(1 + i)(1 - i)} = \dfrac{-1 + i}{2}$
This is not equal to $i$, so statement (A) is FALSE.

Evaluating Option (B):
Given $\omega = \dfrac{-1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2}$, which is a complex cube root of unity, satisfying $\omega^2 + \omega + 1 = 0$ and $\omega^3 = 1$.
$\dfrac{a\omega + b}{c\omega + d} = \dfrac{0 \cdot \omega - 1}{1 \cdot \omega + 1} = \dfrac{-1}{\omega + 1}$
Since $\omega + 1 = -\omega^2$, we have:
$\dfrac{-1}{-\omega^2} = \dfrac{1}{\omega^2} = \dfrac{\omega^3}{\omega^2} = \omega$
Thus, statement (B) is TRUE.

Evaluating Option (C):
The characteristic equation of $ST$ is $\lambda^2 - \text{Tr}(ST)\lambda + \det(ST) = 0$, which gives $\lambda^2 - \lambda + 1 = 0$.
By the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, $(ST)^2 - ST + I = 0$.
Multiplying by $(ST + I)$, we get $(ST)^3 + I = 0 \Rightarrow (ST)^3 = -I$.
Squaring both sides gives $(ST)^6 = I$.
We are given $(ST)^2 = (ST)^m$, which implies $(ST)^{m-2} = I$.
This means $m - 2$ must be a multiple of $6$, so $m = 6k + 2$ for some integer $k$.
For $k = 1$, $m = 8$ (which is a multiple of $8$).
For $k = 2$, $m = 14$ (which is NOT a multiple of $8$).
Thus, statement (C) is FALSE.

Evaluating Option (D):
For $z \in H$, let $z = x + iy$ where $y > 0$.
$\dfrac{az + b}{cz + d} = \dfrac{-1}{z + 1} = \dfrac{-1}{(x + 1) + iy}$
Multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $(x + 1) - iy$:
$\dfrac{-1}{(x + 1) + iy} \times \dfrac{(x + 1) - iy}{(x + 1) - iy} = \dfrac{-(x + 1) + iy}{(x + 1)^2 + y^2}$
The imaginary part of this new complex number is $\dfrac{y}{(x + 1)^2 + y^2}$.
Since $y > 0$ and $(x + 1)^2 + y^2 > 0$, the imaginary part is strictly positive.
Therefore, $\dfrac{az + b}{cz + d} \in H$, making statement (D) TRUE.

Answer: If $\omega = \dfrac{-1 + i\sqrt{3}}{2}$, then $\dfrac{a\omega + b}{c\omega + d} = \omega$; If $z \in H$, then $\dfrac{az + b}{cz + d} \in H$

30497.text: Choose the correct option for the following reactions.
options: '$A$' and '$B$' are both Markovnikov addition products.
'$A$' is Markovnikov product and '$B$' is antiMarkovnikov product.

Markovnikov product.
30497.sol:
In the first step of hydroboration oxidation, the boron and hydrogen add to the same face of the double bond. In the second step, the OH takes the identical position occupied by the boron. Thus, the OH and H groups that are effectively added to the original double bond are cis. The overall addition takes place in anti Markovnikov's fashion.

The reagent is mercury(II) acetate, which dissociates slightly to form $+ Hg ( OAc )$. $+ Hg ( OAc )$ is the electrophile that adds to the pi bond. • The intermediate is a three-membered ring called the mercurinium ion. Overall, the addition of water follows Markovnikov’s rule

The reaction does not suffer from rearrangements because there is no carbocation intermediate.

31868.subject: Chemistry
31868.text: The ratio of mass percentage (w/w) of C : H in a hydrocarbon is $12 : 1$. It has two carbon atoms. The weight (in g) of $CO_2(g)$ formed when $3.38$ g of this hydrocarbon is completely burnt in oxygen is : (Given : Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ C : 12, H : 1, O : 16)
31868.sol:
Ratio of mass percentage of C : H = $12 : 1$

Ratio of moles of C : H = $\dfrac{12}{12} : \dfrac{1}{1} = 1 : 1$

The empirical formula is $CH$. Since the hydrocarbon has two carbon atoms, its molecular formula is $C_2H_2$.

Molar mass of $C_2H_2 = 2 \times 12 + 2 \times 1 = 26$ g mol$^{-1}$

Moles of $C_2H_2$ in $3.38$ g = $\dfrac{3.38}{26} = 0.13$ mol

The combustion reaction is:

$C_2H_2 + \dfrac{5}{2}O_2 \rightarrow 2CO_2 + H_2O$

From the stoichiometry, $1$ mole of $C_2H_2$ produces $2$ moles of $CO_2$.

Moles of $CO_2$ produced = $2 \times 0.13 = 0.26$ mol

Molar mass of $CO_2 = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44$ g mol$^{-1}$

Weight of $CO_2$ formed = $0.26 \times 44 = 11.44$ g

Answer: $11.44$

35670.text: The value of $\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{x^2\sin^2 x}{x^2 - \sin^2 x}\right)$ is:
35670.sol:
Let $L = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x^2\sin^2 x}{x^2 - \sin^2 x}$

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $x^4$, we get:

$L = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\sin x}{x}\right)^2}{\dfrac{x^2 - \sin^2 x}{x^4}}$

Factorizing the denominator:

$L = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\sin x}{x}\right)^2}{\left(\dfrac{x - \sin x}{x^3}\right) \left(\dfrac{x + \sin x}{x}\right)}$

Using the standard limits:

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sin x}{x} = 1$

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x - \sin x}{x^3} = \dfrac{1}{6}$ (using Taylor series expansion $\sin x = x - \dfrac{x^3}{3!} + \dots$)

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{x + \sin x}{x} = \lim_{x \to 0} \left(1 + \dfrac{\sin x}{x}\right) = 1 + 1 = 2$

Substituting these limits into the expression:

$L = \dfrac{1^2}{\left(\dfrac{1}{6}\right) \times 2} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{3}} = 3$

Answer: $3$

36819.subject: Mathematics
36819.text: If $\alpha=1$ and $\beta=1+i\sqrt{2}$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$ are two roots of the equation $x^3+ax^2+bx+c=0$, $a,b,c \in \mathbb{R}$, then $\int_{-1}^{1}(x^3+ax^2+bx+c)dx$ is equal to:
36819.sol:
Since $a, b, c \in \mathbb{R}$, the complex roots of the equation $x^3+ax^2+bx+c=0$ must occur in conjugate pairs.

Given roots are $\alpha = 1$ and $\beta = 1+i\sqrt{2}$.

The third root must be $\gamma = 1-i\sqrt{2}$.

The polynomial is given by:

$x^3+ax^2+bx+c = (x-1)(x-(1+i\sqrt{2}))(x-(1-i\sqrt{2}))$

$= (x-1)((x-1)^2 - (i\sqrt{2})^2)$

$= (x-1)(x^2 - 2x + 1 + 2)$

$= (x-1)(x^2 - 2x + 3)$

$= x^3 - 3x^2 + 5x - 3$

We need to evaluate the integral:

$I = \int_{-1}^{1} (x^3 - 3x^2 + 5x - 3) dx$

Using the property of definite integrals $\int_{-a}^{a} f(x) dx = 0$ for odd functions and $2\int_{0}^{a} f(x) dx$ for even functions:

$I = \int_{-1}^{1} x^3 dx - 3\int_{-1}^{1} x^2 dx + 5\int_{-1}^{1} x dx - 3\int_{-1}^{1} 1 dx$

$I = 0 - 3(2)\int_{0}^{1} x^2 dx + 0 - 3(2)\int_{0}^{1} 1 dx$

$I = -6 \left[ \dfrac{x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{1} - 6 \left[ x \right]_{0}^{1}$

$I = -6 \left( \dfrac{1}{3} \right) - 6(1)$

$I = -2 - 6 = -8$

Answer: $-8$

37143.text: Number of $4$-digit numbers that are less than or equal to $2800$ and either divisible by $3$ or by $11$ , is equal to _____ .
37143.sol:
Four-digit numbers that are less than or equal to $2800$ are $\left\{1000, 1001, 1002, . . . . , 2800\right\}$

Numbers divisible by $3$ are $\left\{1002, 1005, . . . . , 2796, 2799\right\}$

Let total numbers be $n$, then

$1002 + \left(n - 1\right)3 = 2799$

$⇒ n = 600$

Numbers divisible by $11$ are $\left\{1001, 1012, . . . , 2794\right\}$

Let total numbers be $m$, then

$2794 = 1001 + \left(m - 1\right)11$

$⇒ m = 164$

Numbers divisible by $33$ are

$\left\{1023, 1056, . . . , 2772\right\}$

Let total numbers be $r$, then

$2772 = 1023 + \left(r - 1\right)33$

$⇒ r = 54$

Number of $4$-digit numbers that are less than or equal to $2800$ and either divisible by $3$ or by $11$ , is equal to

$= 600 + 164 - 54 = 710$

39913.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The electromagnetic wave exerts pressure on the surface on which they are allowed to fall.
Reason (R): There is no mass associated with the electromagnetic waves.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
39913.sol:
Assertion (A) is true because electromagnetic waves carry energy and momentum. When they strike a surface, they transfer momentum to it, which results in a force and consequently exerts radiation pressure on the surface.

Reason (R) is true because electromagnetic waves consist of photons, which have zero rest mass. Thus, there is no rest mass associated with electromagnetic waves.

However, the pressure exerted by electromagnetic waves is due to the momentum they carry ($p = \dfrac{E}{c}$), not because they are massless. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

40327.text: All electromagnetic wave is transporting energy in the negative $z$ direction. At a certain point and certain time the direction of electric field of the wave is along positive $y$ direction. What will be the direction of the magnetic field of the wave at that point and instant?
40327.sol:
In an electromagnetic wave, the direction of energy flow is along the direction of the wave propagation. Therefore, the wave propagates along negative z direction.

Electric field is along the positive y direction and the wave propagates along negative z direction. Thus, magnetic field is in direction perpendicular to both z and y axes.

Using vector algebra,

$( - \overset{^}{k} ) = ( + \overset{^}{j} ) \times \left(\overset{^}{i}\right)$

Hence, magnetic field is in positive $x$ direction.

40436.subject: Physics
40436.text: A rigid dipole undergoes a simple harmonic motion about its centre in the presence of an electric field $\vec{E}_1=E_0\hat{x}$. If another electric field $\vec{E}_2=2E_0(\hat{y}+\hat{z})$ is introduced to the system, what will be the percentage change in the frequency of the oscillation (approximate)?
40436.sol:
The frequency of oscillation of a rigid dipole in an electric field is given by $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{pE}{I}}$, where $p$ is the dipole moment, $E$ is the magnitude of the electric field, and $I$ is the moment of inertia.

This implies $f \propto \sqrt{E}$.

The initial electric field is $\vec{E}_1 = E_0 \hat{x}$, so its magnitude is $E_1 = E_0$.

The initial frequency is $f_1 \propto \sqrt{E_0}$.

When the second electric field $\vec{E}_2 = 2E_0(\hat{y} + \hat{z})$ is introduced, the net electric field becomes $\vec{E}_{net} = \vec{E}_1 + \vec{E}_2 = E_0 \hat{x} + 2E_0 \hat{y} + 2E_0 \hat{z}$.

The magnitude of the net electric field is $E_{net} = \sqrt{E_0^2 + (2E_0)^2 + (2E_0)^2} = \sqrt{E_0^2 + 4E_0^2 + 4E_0^2} = 3E_0$.

The new frequency is $f_2 \propto \sqrt{3E_0}$.

The percentage change in the frequency is given by $\dfrac{f_2 - f_1}{f_1} \times 100\%$.

Substituting the values, we get $\left( \dfrac{\sqrt{3E_0}}{\sqrt{E_0}} - 1 \right) \times 100\% = (\sqrt{3} - 1) \times 100\%$.

Using $\sqrt{3} \approx 1.732$, the percentage change is $(1.732 - 1) \times 100\% = 73.2\%$.

The approximate percentage change is $73\%$.

Answer: $73\%$

40440.text: Two charged conducting spheres $S_1$ and $S_2$ of radii $8$ cm and $18$ cm are connected to each other by a wire. After equilibrium is established, the ratio of electric fields on $S_1$ and $S_2$ spheres are $E_{S_1}$ and $E_{S_2}$ respectively. The value of $\dfrac{E_{S_1}}{E_{S_2}}$ is _______.

When two conducting spheres are connected by a wire, charge flows until their potentials become equal.

$V_1 = V_2$

$\dfrac{k Q_1}{R_1} = \dfrac{k Q_2}{R_2}$

The electric field on the surface of a conducting sphere is given by $E = \dfrac{k Q}{R^2}$, which can be written as $E = \dfrac{V}{R}$.

Since $V_1 = V_2$, we have:

$E_{S_1} R_1 = E_{S_2} R_2$

$\dfrac{E_{S_1}}{E_{S_2}} = \dfrac{R_2}{R_1}$

Given $R_1 = 8$ cm and $R_2 = 18$ cm:

$\dfrac{E_{S_1}}{E_{S_2}} = \dfrac{18}{8} = \dfrac{9}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{9}{4}$

41259.sol:
Applying Newton's second law along the direction perpendicular to inlined plane:

$N - mgcos{30}^{∘} = 0$ (As $\theta = 30 °$)

(since the acceleration of block in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane is $0$)

$∴ N = mgcos{30}^{∘}$ .....(1)

Let $\mu$ be the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the inclined plane. Applying Newton's second law along inclined plane:

$mgsin{30}^{∘} - \muN = ma = m\dfrac{g}{4}$ ....(2)

(since the acceleration along the inclined plane, $a = \dfrac{g}{4}$)

$∴ mgsin{30}^{∘} - \mumgcos{30}^{∘} = m\dfrac{g}{4}$ (from equation 1 and 2)

$⇒ \dfrac{mg}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\mumg = m\dfrac{g}{4}$

$⇒$$\mu = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}$

42664.subject: Physics
42664.text: The displacement of a particle, executing simple harmonic motion with time period $T$, is expressed as $x(t)=A \sin \omega t$, where $A$ is the amplitude. The maximum value of potential energy of this oscillator is found at $t=T / 2 \beta$. The value of $\beta$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
42664.sol:
For SHM with $x(t) = A\sin(\omega t)$, the potential energy is
$U = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 x^2 = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2 \sin^2(\omega t)$.
Maximum potential energy occurs when $\sin^2(\omega t) = 1$, i.e., when $\omega t = \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}, ...$
The first maximum occurs at $\omega t = \frac{\pi}{2}$, giving $t = \frac{\pi}{2\omega} = \frac{\pi}{2} \cdot \frac{T}{2\pi} = \frac{T}{4}$.
Since this is given as $t = \frac{T}{2\beta}$.
We have $\frac{T}{4} = \frac{T}{2\beta}$, so $\beta = 2$.

43002.text:
A light wave travelling linearly in a medium of dielectric constant $4$, incidents on the horizontal interface separating medium with air. The angle of incidence for which the total intensity of incident wave will be reflected back into the same medium will be :
(Given : relative permeability of medium ${\mu}_{r} = 1$)
43002.sol:
Relative refractive index is $\mu = \sqrt{{\mu}_{r}{ε}_{r}} = \sqrt{4 \times 1} = 2$

Now, for complete reflection, $\theta > {\theta}_{c}$, where, ${\theta}_{c}$ is critical angle.

Now, critical angle is $sin{\theta}_{c} = \dfrac{1}{\mu} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ {\theta}_{c} = \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) ⇒ {\theta}_{c} = 30 °$

So, the angle of incidence for which the total intensity of incident wave will be reflected back into the same medium is $\theta > 30 °$ i.e., $60 °$.

49999.subject: Physics
49999.text: Variation of photoelectric current with anode potential is shown below. Choose the correct option ($V_0$ = stopping potential)
49999.sol:
In the photoelectric effect, the variation of photoelectric current with anode potential has the following characteristics:

1. At zero anode potential, there is still some photoelectric current because the emitted photoelectrons possess initial kinetic energy and can reach the anode.

2. When a negative (retarding) potential is applied to the anode, the photoelectric current decreases. It becomes zero at a specific negative potential known as the stopping potential ($-V_0$).

3. As the positive anode potential is increased, the photoelectric current increases because more electrons are accelerated towards the anode.

4. Eventually, all emitted photoelectrons reach the anode, and the current reaches a maximum constant value called the saturation current. Further increasing the anode potential does not increase the current.

Graph-I correctly depicts all these features: it starts from zero at the stopping potential on the negative x-axis, has a positive value at zero potential, and flattens out to a constant saturation current at higher positive potentials.

Answer:

Therefore,

55440.subject: Chemistry
55440.text: Which from following compounds is used to prepare adipic acid, enzymatically in Green technology developed by Darth and Frost?
55440.sol:
In the green technology developed by Draths and Frost, adipic acid is synthesized using D-glucose as the starting material.

The process involves the use of genetically engineered bacteria (E. coli) to convert glucose into cis,cis-muconic acid through a biocatalytic pathway. The cis,cis-muconic acid is subsequently hydrogenated under mild conditions to produce adipic acid.

This method provides an environmentally friendly alternative to the traditional synthesis of adipic acid, which relies on petroleum-based benzene and generates nitrous oxide (a greenhouse gas) as a byproduct.

Answer: Glucose

56352.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
56352.text: What happens to the size of atoms in p-block elements when we move from left to right in the same period?
56352.sol:
As we move from left to right across a period, the atomic number increases, meaning the number of protons in the nucleus increases.

The additional electrons are added to the same principal shell, so the shielding effect remains almost constant.

This results in an increase in the effective nuclear charge (Z_{eff}$), which pulls the valence electrons closer to the nucleus.

Consequently, the atomic size decreases from left to right in the same period.

Answer: Size decreases$

56833.subject: Chemistry
56833.text: Identify from following cell reactions that is spontaneous under standard state of conditions.
56833.sol:
For a cell reaction to be spontaneous under standard conditions, the standard cell potential $E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}}$ must be positive.

$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{anode}}$

Evaluating the given options:

For $\text{Ca(s)} + \text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + \text{Cd(s)}$:
Cathode (reduction): $\text{Cd}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Cd}$
Anode (oxidation): $\text{Ca} \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+}$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = -0.403 - (-2.866) = +2.463 \text{ V}$ (Spontaneous)

For $2\text{Br}^-\text{(s)} + \text{Sn}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Br}_2\text{(l)} + \text{Sn(s)}$:
Cathode: $\text{Sn}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Sn}$
Anode: $2\text{Br}^- \rightarrow \text{Br}_2$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = -0.136 - 1.08 = -1.216 \text{ V}$ (Non-spontaneous)

For $2\text{Ag(s)} + \text{Ni}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\text{Ag}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{Ni(s)}$:
Cathode: $\text{Ni}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Ni}$
Anode: $\text{Ag} \rightarrow \text{Ag}^+$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = -0.257 - 0.799 = -1.056 \text{ V}$ (Non-spontaneous)

For $2\text{Au(s)} + \text{Zn}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\text{Au}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{Zn(s)}$:
Cathode: $\text{Zn}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Zn}$
Anode: $\text{Au} \rightarrow \text{Au}^+$
$E^{{}^{\circ}}_{\text{cell}} = -0.763 - 1.68 = -2.443 \text{ V}$ (Non-spontaneous)

The only reaction with a positive standard cell potential is the first one.

Answer: $\text{Ca(s)} + \text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + \text{Cd(s)}$, $[E^0_{\text{Ca}} = -2.866$ V $E^0_{\text{Cd}} = -0.403$ V$]$

60274.subject: Mathematics
60274.text: The function $x^5-5 x^4+5 x^3-10$ has a maximum, when $x$ is equal to
60274.sol:
Critical points of $f(x) = x^5 - 5x^4 + 5x^3 - 10$ are found where the first derivative vanishes.

The derivative is $f'(x) = 5x^4 - 20x^3 + 15x^2$, which factors as $5x^2(x-1)(x-3)$.
Setting $f'(x) = 0$ yields critical values at $x = 0$, $x = 1$, and $x = 3$.

The second derivative is $f''(x) = 20x^3 - 60x^2 + 30x$.
At $x = 1$, $f''(1) = -10 < 0$, indicating a local maximum.
At $x = 3$, $f''(3) = 90 > 0$, indicating a local minimum.
At $x = 0$, $f'(x)$ does not change sign, identifying it as an inflection point.

The maximum occurs at $x = 1$.

60724.subject: Mathematics
60724.text: The number of common tangents to the circles $x^2+y^2-4 x-6 y-12=0$ and $x^2+y^2+6 x+18 y+26=0$, is
60724.sol:
The centers and radii of the circles are determined by completing the square or comparing with the general circle equation.

For $S_1: x^2+y^2-4 x-6 y-12=0$, center is $C_1 = (2,3)$ and radius $r_1 = 5$.

For $S_2: x^2+y^2+6 x+18 y+26=0$, center is $C_2 = (-3,-9)$ and radius $r_2 = 8$.

The distance between centers is $d = \sqrt{(-3-2)^2 + (-9-3)^2} = 13$.

Since $d = r_1 + r_2 = 5 + 8 = 13$, the circles touch externally.

Two externally tangent circles have exactly three common tangents.

Answer: $3$

61271.subject: Mathematics
61271.text: The differential equation of the family of all parabolas whose axis is the $y$-axis is $\ldots$
61271.sol:
The equation of the family of all parabolas whose axis is the $y$-axis is given by:

$y = ax^2 + c$

where $a$ and $c$ are arbitrary constants.

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2ax$

$\Rightarrow 2a = \dfrac{1}{x} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$, we get:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2a$

Substituting the value of $2a$ from the first derivative into the second derivative, we get:

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{1}{x} \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$\Rightarrow x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

Answer: $x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

Consider the function $\mathrm{f}(x)=\cot^{-1} $\$left(\frac{x^x-x^{-x}}{2}\right). The derivative at $x=1$ follows from the chain rule and derivative of the argument.

Let u(x)=\frac{x^x-x^{-x}}{2}. Then $$\mathrm{f}$'$(x)=\frac{-1}{1+u^2}\cdot$u'(x)$.

The derivatives of $x^x$ and $x^{-x}$ are found via logarithmic differentiation: \frac{d}{dx}$x^x=x^x(1+\ln x)$ and \frac{d}{dx}$x^{-x}=-x^{-x}(1+\ln x)$.

Thus, the derivative of $u(x)$ is: $u'$(x)=\frac{1}{2}\left[$x^x(1+\ln x)+x^{-x}(1+\ln x)\$right]=\frac{1}{2}($1+\ln x)(x^x+x^{-x})$.

At $x=1$, we compute: u(1)=\frac{1^1-1^{-1}}{2}=$0$ and $u'$(1)=\frac{1}{2}($1+\ln $1)(1^1+1^{-1})=\frac{1}{2}($1)(2)=1$.

Therefore, $$\mathrm{f}$'$(1)=\frac{-1}{1+0^2}\cdot$1=-1$.

The value is $\boxed{$\text{A}$}$.

$

63448.subject: Mathematics
63448.text: The distance of the focus of the parabola $y^2 = 16x$ from its directrix is...
63448.sol:
The given equation of the parabola is $y^2 = 16x$.

Comparing this with the standard form $y^2 = 4ax$, we get $4a = 16$, which gives $a = 4$.

The coordinates of the focus are $(a, 0) = (4,0)$.

The equation of the directrix is $x = -a$, which is $x = -4$.

The distance between the focus and the directrix is the perpendicular distance from the point $(4,0)$ to the line $x + 4 = 0$.

Distance $= |4 - (-4)| = 8$.

Alternatively, the distance from the focus to the directrix for a parabola $y^2 = 4ax$ is always $2a$.

Distance $= 2 \times 4 = 8$.

Answer: $8$

64833.subject: Mathematics
64833.text: If $1-\cos \theta=\sin \theta \cdot \sin \frac{\theta}{2}$, then the value of $\theta$ is
64833.sol:
Beginning with $1-\cos\theta = \sin\theta \cdot \sin\frac{\theta}{2}$, apply the half-angle identity $1-\cos\theta = 2\sin^2\frac{\theta}{2}$ and the double-angle identity $\sin\theta = 2\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\cos\frac{\theta}{2}$ to rewrite the equation:

$2\sin^2\frac{\theta}{2} = 2\sin^2\frac{\theta}{2}\cos\frac{\theta}{2}$

Subtract the right side and factor:

$2\sin^2\frac{\theta}{2}(1-\cos\frac{\theta}{2}) = 0$

This implies either $\sin\frac{\theta}{2} = 0$ or $\cos\frac{\theta}{2} = 1$.

The solution $\sin\frac{\theta}{2} = 0$ yields $\frac{\theta}{2} = n\pi$ or $\theta = 2n\pi$ for integer $n$.

The solution $\cos\frac{\theta}{2} = 1$ yields $\frac{\theta}{2} = 2k\pi$ or $\theta = 4k\pi$ for integer $k$.

Since all values of the form $4k\pi$ are already contained in the set $2n\pi$, the general solution is $\theta = 2n\pi$ for integer $n$.

Comparing with the options, only option A includes this solution set.

66069.text: A series combination of 10 capacitors, each of value ' $\mathrm{C}_1$ ' is charged by a source of potential difference ' 4 V '. When another parallel combination of 8 capacitors, each of value ' $\mathrm{C}_2$ ' is charged by a source of potential difference ' $V$ ', it has the same total energy stored in it as in the first combination. The value of ' $\mathrm{C}_2$ ' is
66069.sol:
The equivalent capacitance of 10 identical capacitors $C_1$ in series is $C_{eq1} = \frac{C_1}{10}$.

When charged to $4V$, the stored energy becomes $U_1 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{C_1}{10} \cdot (4V)^2 = \frac{4}{5} C_1 V^2$.

For 8 capacitors $C_2$ in parallel, the equivalent capacitance is $C_{eq2} = 8C_2$.

The stored energy at voltage $V$ is $U_2 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 8C_2 \cdot V^2 = 4C_2 V^2$.

Equating the energies yields $\frac{4}{5} C_1 V^2 = 4C_2 V^2$, which simplifies to $C_2 = \frac{C_1}{5}$.

This corresponds to option A.

66766.text: In the given circuit, if $dI/dt = -1\ \text{A/s}$ then the value of $V_{AB}$ at this instant will be
66766.sol:
Applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) from point A to point B:

$V_A - IR - L \dfrac{dI}{dt} - V_{\text{battery}} = V_B$

Given:
$I = 2\ \text{A}$
$R = 6\ \Omega$
$L = 3\ \text{H}$
$\dfrac{dI}{dt} = -1\ \text{A/s}$
$V_{\text{battery}} = 6\ \text{V}$ (Moving from left to right along the bottom wire, the path goes from the positive to the negative terminal, so it is a potential drop)

Substituting the values into the KVL equation:

$V_A - (2)(6) - (3)(-1) - 6 = V_B$

$V_A - 12 + 3 - 6 = V_B$

$V_A - 15 = V_B$

$V_{AB} = V_A - V_B = 15\ \text{V}$

Answer: $15\text{V}$

Summing all contributions yields:

67221.text: A pendulum is oscillating with frequency ' $n$ ' on the surface of earth. If it is taken to a depth $\frac{{ }^{\prime} \mathrm{R}^{\prime}}{3}$ below the surface of earth, new frequency of oscillation is ( $R=$ radius of earth)
67221.sol:
The frequency of oscillation of a simple pendulum is given by
$n = \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{g}{L}}$, where $g$ is gravitational acceleration and $L$ is the pendulum length. At depth $d = \frac{R}{3}$ below Earth's surface, the reduced gravitational acceleration is
$g' = g\left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right) = g\left(1 - \frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{2}{3}g$.

The new frequency becomes
$n' = \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{g'}{L}} = \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{2g}{3L}} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} \cdot \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{g}{L}}$.

Since $\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{g}{L}} = n$, it follows that
$n' = \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}n$.

The result corresponds to option A.

67691.subject: Physics
67691.text: A particle of charge $q$ moves with a velocity $\vec{V}=$ ai in a magnetic field $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{b} \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\mathrm{ck}$, where ' a ', ' b ' and ' c ' are constants. The magnitude of force experienced by particle is
67691.sol:
The magnetic force on a charged particle is given by the Lorentz force law: $\vec{F} = q (\vec{V} \times \vec{B})$.

Given $\vec{V} = a\hat{i}$ and $\vec{B} = b\hat{j} + c\hat{k}$, the cross product is computed as:

$\vec{V} \times \vec{B} = (a\hat{i}) \times (b\hat{j} + c\hat{k}) = ab(\hat{i} \times \hat{j}) + ac(\hat{i} \times \hat{k})$.

Using the identities $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$ and $\hat{i} \times \hat{k} = -\hat{j}$, the result simplifies to:

$\vec{V} \times \vec{B} = ab\hat{k} - ac\hat{j}$.

Substituting back into the force equation yields:

$\vec{F} = q(ab\hat{k} - ac\hat{j}) = -qac\hat{j} + qab\hat{k}$.

The magnitude is found using the Euclidean norm:

$|\vec{F}| = \sqrt{(-qac)^2 + (qab)^2} = \sqrt{q^2 a^2 c^2 + q^2 a^2 b^2} = |qa| \sqrt{b^2 + c^2}$.

For physical quantities, we take absolute values, giving $|\vec{F}| = qa \sqrt{b^2 + c^2}$, which corresponds to option A.

Final Answer: $\boxed{\text{A}}$

68027.text: A wire has a mass $0.3 \pm 0.003$ gram, radius $0.5 \pm 0.005 \mathrm{ mm}$ and length $6 \pm 0.06 \mathrm{ cm}$. The maximum percentage error in the measurement of its density is
68027.sol:
The density $\rho$ of a cylinder is given by $\rho = M / (\pi r^2 L)$, where $M$ is mass, $r$ is radius, and $L$ is length. For error propagation in a function of the form $X = A^a B^b C^c$, the maximum fractional error is $\Delta X / X = a (\Delta A / A) + b (\Delta B / B) + c (\Delta C / C)$.

Rewriting density as $\rho \propto M^1 r^{-2} L^{-1}$ with $\pi$ being constant, the percentage error is $\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100\% = \left(1 \cdot \frac{\Delta M}{M} + 2 \cdot \frac{\Delta r}{r} + 1 \cdot \frac{\Delta L}{L}\right) \times 100\%$.

Substituting the reported errors, each term has 1% error: $\frac{\Delta M}{M} = 1\%$, $\frac{\Delta r}{r} = 1\%$, $\frac{\Delta L}{L} = 1\%$. Therefore, the percentage error is $(1\% + 2 \cdot 1\% + 1\%) = 4\%$.

Maximum percentage error in density: $4\%$

68605.subject: Physics
68605.text: A radioactive element having half-life 30 min. is undergoing beta decay. The fraction of radioactive element remains undecayed after 90 min. will be
68605.sol:
The fraction of radioactive material remaining after time $t$ is determined by the decay formula:

$\frac{N}{N_0} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/T_{1/2}}$

Given a half-life $T_{1/2} = 30\ \text\min$ and time $t = 90\ \text\min$, the elapsed time spans $3$ half-lives.

Substituting into the decay law yields:

$\frac{N}{N_0} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{8}$

The fraction remaining undecayed is therefore $\frac{1}{8}$.

68662.subject: Physics
68662.text: A light spring is suspended with mass '$m_1$' at its lower end and its upper end is fixed to a rigid support. The mass is pulled down a short distance and then released. The period of oscillation is T second. When a mass '$m_2$' is added to '$m_1$' and the system is made to oscillate the period is found to be $\dfrac{3}{2}$ T. The ratio $\left(\dfrac{m_1}{m_2}\right)$ is
68662.sol:
The time period of a spring-mass system is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}}$, where $m$ is the mass and $k$ is the spring constant.

For the initial case with mass $m_1$:
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m_1}{k}}$

When mass $m_2$ is added, the total mass becomes $m_1 + m_2$ and the new time period is $\dfrac{3}{2}T$:
$\dfrac{3}{2}T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{m_1 + m_2}{k}}$

Dividing the second equation by the first equation:
$\dfrac{3}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m_1 + m_2}{m_1}}$

Squaring both sides:
$\dfrac{9}{4} = \dfrac{m_1 + m_2}{m_1}$

$\dfrac{9}{4} = 1 + \dfrac{m_2}{m_1}$

$\dfrac{m_2}{m_1} = \dfrac{9}{4} - 1 = \dfrac{5}{4}$

Taking the reciprocal to find the required ratio:
$\dfrac{m_1}{m_2} = \dfrac{4}{5}$

The ratio is $4 : 5$.

Answer: $4 : 5$

70199.text: According to Huygen's wave theory of light, which one of the following statements is <u>not</u> correct?
options: Different colours of light are due to different wavelengths of waves.
Different colours of light are due to different sizes of the corpuscles.
Speed of light in denser medium is less than that in rarer medium.

70199.sol:
Huygen's wave theory postulates that light propagates as waves rather than particles. Statement B is inconsistent with this theory as it attributes color differences to "sizes of corpuscles," a concept from Newton's corpuscular theory rather than wave theory.

Statement A aligns with wave theory, as different wavelengths correspond to different colors of light. Statement C is a key prediction of Huygen's theory: light travels slower in denser media than in rarer media. Statement D reflects the theory's success in deriving the laws of reflection and refraction.

The statement not correct according to Huygen's wave theory is B.

70502.text: Two waves of same frequency (n) are approaching each other with same velocity of $12 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ along the same linear path and interfere. The distance between two consecutive nodes is
70502.sol:
Standing waves form when two waves of identical frequency and amplitude travel in opposite directions, with nodes being points of zero displacement.

The wave relationship $v = n\lambda$ connects velocity, frequency, and wavelength. Given $v = 12$ m/s, the wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{12}{n}$ m.

For standing waves, consecutive nodes are separated by half the wavelength, so the distance is $\frac{\lambda}{2} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{12}{n} = \frac{6}{n}$ m.

The correct choice is $\frac{6}{n}$.

70901.subject: Biology
70901.text: In Plasmodium, which causes malaria, fertilization of gametocytes takes place in ____.
options: salivary glands of a female Anopheles mosquito
70901.sol:
In the life cycle of Plasmodium, gametocytes are formed in the red blood cells of the human host.

When a female Anopheles mosquito takes a blood meal from an infected person, these gametocytes enter the mosquito's gut.

Inside the gut (stomach) of the mosquito, the gametocytes mature into male and female gametes. Fertilization occurs here, leading to the formation of a diploid zygote.

The zygote then develops into a motile ookinete, which penetrates the gut wall to form an oocyst.

Answer: gut of a female Anopheles mosquito

71676.subject: Chemistry
71676.text: Which of the following is Zwitter ion of sulphanilic acid?
71676.sol:
Sulphanilic acid is $p$-aminobenzenesulphonic acid, which contains both an acidic group ($-SO_3H$) and a basic group ($-NH_2$).

In aqueous solution or in the solid state, the acidic $-SO_3H$ group donates a proton (H^+$) to the basic $-NH_2$ group. This internal acid-base reaction leads to the formation of a dipolar ion, known as a zwitterion.

The resulting zwitterion has a positively charged ammonium group ($-NH_3^+$) and a negatively charged sulphonate group ($-SO_3^-$) at the para positions of the benzene ring.

Looking at the given options, the structure with $-NH_3^+$ and $-SO_3^-$ at para positions represents the zwitterion of sulphanilic acid.

Answer:$

71827.subject: Chemistry
71827.text: Which of the following alkyl halides gives a mixture of alkenes on dehydrohalogenation?
71827.sol:
Dehydrohalogenation of alkyl halides involves the removal of a hydrogen atom from a $\beta$-carbon and a halogen atom from the $\alpha$-carbon to form an alkene.

For n-propyl bromide (CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-Br$), there is only one \beta$-carbon, yielding only propene.

For isopropyl bromide (CH_3-CH(Br)-CH_3$), the two \beta$-carbons are equivalent, yielding only propene.

For secondary butyl bromide (CH_3-CH_2-CH(Br)-CH_3$), there are two non-equivalent \beta$-carbons. Elimination of hydrogen from these different $\beta$-carbons yields a mixture of 1-butene and 2-butene (which further exists as cis and trans isomers).

For tertiary butyl bromide ($(CH_3)_3C-Br$), all three $\beta$-carbons are equivalent, yielding only 2-methylpropene.

Thus, secondary butyl bromide gives a mixture of alkenes.

Answer: Secondary butyl bromide

71933.subject: Chemistry
71933.text: Which of the following formulae is used to find total volume of atoms present in face-centred cubic unit cell?
71933.sol:
In a face-centred cubic (fcc) unit cell, the total number of atoms per unit cell is $Z = 4$.

Assuming each atom is a sphere of radius $r$, the volume of one atom is $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.

Total volume of atoms present in the fcc unit cell $= Z \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.

Total volume $= 4 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \dfrac{16}{3}\pi r^3$.

Answer: $\dfrac{16}{3}\pi r^3$

72029.subject: Chemistry
72029.text: Identify a correct set of quantum numbers that represents the highest energy of an electron in an orbital from following.
72029.sol:
The energy of an electron in a multi-electron atom is determined by the $(n + l)$ rule. A higher value of $(n + l)$ corresponds to a higher energy level. If two orbitals have the same $(n + l)$ value, the one with the higher $n$ value has higher energy.

Calculating $(n + l)$ for the given options:

For $n = 3, l = 0$: $n + l = 3 + 0 = 3$

For $n = 3, l = 1$: $n + l = 3 + 1 = 4$

For $n = 3, l = 2$: $n + l = 3 + 2 = 5$

For $n = 4, l = 0$: $n + l = 4 + 0 = 4$

The maximum value of $(n + l)$ is $5$, which corresponds to the $3d$ orbital. Thus, the set of quantum numbers $n = 3, l = 2, m_l = +1, s = +1/2$ represents the highest energy.

Answer: $n = 3 , l = 2 , m_l = +1 , s = + 1/2$

72039.subject: Chemistry
72039.text: The bond enthalpies of H-H, Cl-Cl, and H-Cl bonds are 437 kJ/mol, 239 kJ/mol, and 433 kJ/mol respectively. Calculate the enthalpy of formation of HCl.
72039.sol:
The reaction for the formation of HCl is:

$\dfrac{1}{2} \text{H}_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2} \text{Cl}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{HCl}(g)$

The enthalpy of formation $\Delta H_f$ is given by the difference between the bond enthalpies of reactants and products:

$\Delta H_f = \sum \text{BE}(\text{reactants}) - \sum \text{BE}(\text{products})$

$\Delta H_f = \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \text{BE}(\text{H-H}) + \dfrac{1}{2} \text{BE}(\text{Cl-Cl}) \right) - \text{BE}(\text{H-Cl})$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H_f = \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \times 437 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 239 \right) - 433$

$\Delta H_f = (218.5 + 119.5) - 433$

$\Delta H_f = 338 - 433 = -95 \text{ kJ/mol}$

Answer: $-95$ kJ/mol

73919.text:
Paragraph: The grouping or assemblage of plants, animals and microbes we observe when we study a natural forest, a grassland, a pond, a coral reef or some other undisturbed area, is referred to as the area's biota or biotic community. The plant portion of the biotic community includes all vegetation, from large trees down through to microscopic algae. Likewise, the animal portion includes everything from large mammals, birds, reptiles and amphibians through to earthworms, tiny insects and mites. Microbes encompass a large array of microscopic bacteria, fungi and protozoans. Thus, the biotic community comprises a plant community, an animal community and a microbial community. The particular kind of biotic community found in a given area is, in large part, determined by abiotic factors such as the amount of water or moisture present, the temperature, the salinity, or the type of soil in the areThese abiotic factors both support and limit the particular community. For example, a relative lack of available moisture prevents the growth of most species of plants, but supports certain species, such as cacti; these kinds of areas are deserts. Land with plenty of available moisture and a suitable temperature supports forests. The presence of water is the major factor that sustains aquatic communities. The first step in investigating a biotic community may be simply to catalogue all the species present. Species are the different kinds of plants, animals and microbes in the community. A given species includes all those individuals which have a strong similarity in appearance to one another and which are distinct in appearance from other such groups. Each species in a biotic community is represented by a certain population - that is, by a certain number of individuals that make up the interbreeding, reproducing group.
Question: The nature of the biotic community largely depends on: 1. Biotic components 2. Abiotic components Select the correct answer using the code given below:

The recoil velocity of gun $=-\mathrm{3 m} / \mathrm{s}$

76400.subject: Mathematics
76400.text: Where does the function $f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^7(x-j)^2$ attain its minimum value $?$
76400.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
& f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^7(x-j)^2=\sum_{j=1}^7\left(x^2-2 x j+j^2\right) \\
& x^2 \sum_{j=1}^7 1-2 x \sum_{j=1}^7 j+\sum_{j=1}^7 j^2 \\
& =7 x^2-2 x \frac{7(7+1)}{2}+\frac{7(7+1)(14+1)}{6} \\
& =7 x^2-56 x+140 \\
& f^{\prime}(x)=14 x-56=0 \Rightarrow x=4 \\
& f^{\prime \prime}(x)=14 \gt 0
\end{aligned}\therefore \quad f(x)$ is minimum at $x=4$.

76715.subject: Mathematics
76715.text:
For the following two (02) items:
Let the function $f(x) = |x - 3| + |x - 4|$ be defined on the interval $[0,5]$.

Consider the following statements:
I. The function is differentiable at $x = 3$.
II. The function is differentiable at $x = 4$.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
76715.sol:
The given function is $f(x) = |x - 3| + |x - 4|$ defined on $[0,5]$.

We can redefine the function by removing the absolute value signs in different intervals:

$f(x) = \begin{cases} -(x - 3) - (x - 4), & 0 \le x < 3 \\ (x - 3) - (x - 4), & 3 \le x < 4 \\ (x - 3) + (x - 4), & 4 \le x \le 5 \end{cases}$

Simplifying this, we get:

$f(x) = \begin{cases} 7 - 2x, & 0 \le x < 3 \\ 1, & 3 \le x < 4 \\ 2x - 7, & 4 \le x \le 5 \end{cases}$

Differentiating $f(x)$ with respect to $x$ in the open intervals:

$f'(x) = \begin{cases} -2, & 0 < x < 3 \\ 0, & 3 < x < 4 \\ 2, & 4 < x < 5 \end{cases}$

At $x = 3$:
Left Hand Derivative (LHD) $= -2$
Right Hand Derivative (RHD) $= 0$
Since LHD \neq RHD, $ f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 3$.

At $x = 4$:
Left Hand Derivative (LHD) $= 0$
Right Hand Derivative (RHD) $= 2$
Since LHD \neq RHD, $ f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 4$.

Therefore, neither statement I nor statement II is correct.

Answer: Neither I nor II

78954.subject: Mathematics
78954.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let $p = |\sin\alpha - \sin(\alpha - 90°)|$.

What is the minimum value of $p$?
78954.sol:
$p = |\sin\alpha - \sin(\alpha - 90^{}^{\circ})|$

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin(\alpha - 90^{}^{\circ}) = -\sin(90^{}^{\circ} - \alpha) = -\cos\alpha$, we get:

$p = |\sin\alpha - (-\cos\alpha)| = |\sin\alpha + \cos\alpha|$

Multiplying and dividing the expression inside the modulus by $\sqrt{2}:

$p = $\sqrt{2}\left| \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin\alpha + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos\alpha \right|$

$p = \sqrt{2} |\sin(\alpha + 45^{}^{\circ})|$

Since the absolute value of any real expression is non-negative, the minimum possible value of $p$ is $0$. This minimum is achieved when \sin(\alpha + 45^{}^{\circ}) = 0$, which occurs at \alpha = -45^{}^{\circ}$.

Therefore, the minimum value of $p$ is $0$.

84504.subject: Zoology
84504.text: Which of the following is not an autoimmune disease?
84504.sol:
An autoimmune disease is a condition in which your immune system mistakenly attacks your body.
The immune system normally guards against germs like bacteria and viruses. When it senses these foreign invaders, it sends out an army of fighter cells to attack them.
Normally, the immune system can tell the difference between foreign cells and your own cells.
In an autoimmune disease, the immune system mistakes part of your body — like your joints or skin — as foreign. Thus, it loses its ability to differentiate between the self and non-self antigens. In response to these antigens, it releases proteins called antibodies that attack healthy cells.

Ex- Rheumatoid arthritis, Psoriasis, vitiligo

Alzheimer's disease is not an autoimmune disease. It is a progressive disorder caused by a combination of genetic, lifestyle and environmental factors that affect the brain over time. People suffering from Alzheimer's disease have a difficulty in remembering day to day activities, eventually leading to dementia.

$4Al + 3{O}_{2} \to 2A{l}_{2}{O}_{3}$

89158.text: A metal crystallizes into two cubic systems-face centred cubic (fcc) and simple cubic (SC), whose unit cell lengths are $\text{4}\text{.5}$ and $\text{1}\text{.5}\overset{o}{A}$ respectively. Calculate the ratio of densities of face centred cubic and Simple cubic.
89158.sol:
face centred cubic unit cell length $\text{=}\text{4}\text{.5}\overset{o}{A}$
Simple cubic unit cell length $\text{=}\text{1}\text{.5}\overset{o}{A}$
Density in face centred cubic $= \dfrac{{n}_{1} \times atomicweight}{{V}_{1} \times Avogadronumber}$
Density simple cubic (SC) $= \dfrac{{n}_{2} \times atomicmass}{{V}_{2} \times Avogardronumber}$
$\dfrac{{D}_{fcc}}{{D}_{bcc}} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}}{{n}_{2}} \times \dfrac{{V}_{2}}{{V}_{1}}$
${n}_{1}$ for face centred cubic = 4; Also ${V}_{1} = a^{3} = {\left(4.5 \times {10}^{- 8}\right)}^{3}$
${n}_{2}$ for simple cubic = 1; Also ${V}_{2} = a^{3} = {\left(1.5 \times {10}^{- 8}\right)}^{3}$
$\dfrac{{D}_{fcc}}{{D}_{sc}} = \dfrac{4 \times ( 1.5 \times 1{0}^{- 8}{)}^{3}}{1 \times ( 4.5 \times 1{0}^{- 8}{)}^{3}} = 0.15$

91100.text: The value(s) of $x$ satisfying the equation $\sin^{-1} ⁡ \left(1 - x\right) - 2\sin^{-1} ⁡ x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$& is/are
91100.sol:
We have,
${sin}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - x\right) - 2{sin}^{- 1} ⁡ x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$
$⇒ {sin}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - x\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + 2{sin}^{- 1} ⁡ x$
$⇒ 1 - x = sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + 2{sin}^{- 1} ⁡ x\right)$
$⇒ 1 - x = cos ⁡ \left(2{sin}^{- 1} ⁡ x\right)$
$⇒ 1 - x = cos ⁡ \left\{{cos}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - 2{x}^{2}\right)\right\}\left[∵ 2{sin}^{- 1} ⁡ x = {cos}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - 2{x}^{2}\right)\right]$
$⇒ 1 - x = \left(1 - 2{x}^{2}\right)$
$⇒ x = 2{x}^{2} ⇒ x\left(2x - 1\right) = 0 ⇒ x = 0, \dfrac{1}{2}$
For, $x = \dfrac{1}{2},$ we have
LHS $= {sin}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - x\right) - 2{sin}^{- 1} ⁡ x$
$= {sin}^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{1}{2} - 2{sin}^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{1}{2} = - {sin}^{- 1} ⁡ \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{- \pi}{6} \ne R . H . S .$
So, $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ is not a root of the given equation.
Clearly, $x = 0$ satisfies the equation
Here, $x = 0$ is the root of the given equation.

92958.text:
Consider the two following statements I and II, and identify the correct choice given in the answers
1. In photovoltaic cells, the photoelectric current produced is not proportional to the intensity of incident light.
2. In gas-filled photoemissive cells, the velocity of photoelectrons depends on the wavelength of the incident radiation.
92958.sol:
In photovoltaic cells, photoelectric current produced is proportional to the intensity of incident light, so the statement $1$ is false.

The velocity of photoelectrons depends upon the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons, which depends on the frequency and hence on the wavelength of incident radiation, so the statement $2$ is true.

R.H.Whittaker gave the five-kingdom classification i.e. Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia. They are present everywhere. Some bacteria help in nitrogen fixation. Example: Rhizobium. Some bacteria live in hot sulfur springs and they obtain their energy by reduction of sulfur. Fungi are heterotrophic and saprophyte.

100031.subject: Physics
100031.text: In an experiment, a student measures the time period of a simple pendulum five times. The recorded values are $2.63 \mathrm{~s}$, $2.56 \mathrm{~s}$, $2.42 \mathrm{~s}$, $2.71 \mathrm{~s}$, and $2.80 \mathrm{~s}$. The mean time period rounded to the appropriate number of significant figures is:
100031.sol:
The sum of the measured time periods is:
$2.63 + 2.56 + 2.42 + 2.71 + 2.80 = 13.12 \mathrm{~s}$

The mean time period is calculated by dividing the sum by the exact number of measurements (5):
Mean $= \dfrac{13.12}{5} = 2.624 \mathrm{~s}$

Since the original measurements are recorded to two decimal places, the final result must also be rounded to two decimal places.

Rounding $2.624 \mathrm{~s}$ to two decimal places gives $2.62 \mathrm{~s}$.

Answer: $2.62 \mathrm{~s}$

100130.subject: Physics
100130.text: If pressure $[P]$, velocity $[V]$ and time $[T]$ are chosen as the fundamental physical quantities, what will be the dimensional formula of force?
100130.sol:
Let $[Force] = [P]^a [V]^b [T]^c$

Substituting the standard dimensional formulas for each quantity:
$[MLT^{-2}] = [ML^{-1}T^{-2}]^a [LT^{-1}]^b [T]^c$
$[MLT^{-2}] = [M^a L^{-a+b} T^{-2a-b+c}]$

Comparing the powers of $M$, $L$, and $T$ on both sides:
For $M$: $a = 1$
For $L$: $-a + b = 1 \Rightarrow -1 + b = 1 \Rightarrow b = 2$
For $T$: $-2a - b + c = -2 \Rightarrow -2(1) - 2 + c = -2 \Rightarrow -4 + c = -2 \Rightarrow c = 2$

Therefore, the dimensional formula of force in this new system is $[P][V]^2[T]^2$.

Answer: $[P][V]^2[T]^2$

103727.subject: Physics
103727.text: A positive ion is moving with a speed of $5 \times 10^5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ parallel to an infinitely long straight wire carrying a current of $20 \text{ A}$. The perpendicular distance between the ion and the wire is $5 \text{ cm}$. In order to keep the ion moving undeflected in its original path, a uniform electric field must be applied in the region. What is the required magnitude of this electric field?
103727.sol:
For the ion to move undeflected, the net force on it must be zero. This means the electric force must exactly balance the magnetic force in magnitude and be opposite in direction.

The condition for undeflected motion is:
$qE = qvB$
$E = vB$

The magnetic field $B$ produced by a long straight wire at a distance $r$ is:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$

Given:
$I = 20 \text{ A}$
$r = 5 \text{ cm} = 0.05 \text{ m}$
$v = 5 \times 10^5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

Calculating $B$:
$B = \dfrac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 20}{2\pi \times 0.05} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-7} \times 20}{0.05} = 8 \times 10^{-5} \text{ T}$

Now, calculate the required electric field $E$:
$E = vB = (5 \times 10^5) \times (8 \times 10^{-5}) = 40 \text{ V m}^{-1}$

Note: Using the formula for a circular loop $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2r}$ leads to the incorrect answer $40\pi \text{ V m}^{-1}$.

Answer: $40 \text{ V m}^{-1}$

The electromagnetic waves used for studying crystal structures are X-rays.

104502.subject: Physics
104502.text: An equiconcave lens is made of glass with a refractive index of $1.5$. If the radius of curvature of each of its surfaces is $20\text{ cm}$, what is the power of the lens?
104502.sol:
For an equiconcave lens, the radii of curvature are $R_1 = -20\text{ cm}$ and $R_2 = +20\text{ cm}$.

Using the Lens Maker's formula:
$\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$

Substitute the given values:
$\dfrac{1}{f} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{-20} - \dfrac{1}{20}\right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f} = 0.5 \times \left(-\dfrac{2}{20}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

The focal length is $f = -20\text{ cm} = -0.2\text{ m}$.

The power of the lens is given by $P = \dfrac{1}{f(\text{in m})}$.

$P = \dfrac{1}{-0.2} = -5\text{ D}$.

Answer: $-5\text{ D}$

117088.subject: Chemistry
117088.text: Which of the following transition metal ions has a calculated spin-only magnetic moment of $5.92 \text{ BM}$?
117088.sol:
The spin-only magnetic moment is given by the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM}$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given $\mu = 5.92 \text{ BM}$, we can find $n$ by approximating $\sqrt{n(n+2)} \approx 5.92$. Since $\sqrt{35} \approx 5.916$, we have $n(n+2) = 35$, which gives $n = 5$ unpaired electrons.

Now, let us evaluate the number of unpaired electrons for each given ion:

$\text{Fe}^{2+}$ (Atomic number $26$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6 \Rightarrow 4$ unpaired electrons.

$\text{Mn}^{2+}$ (Atomic number $25$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5 \Rightarrow 5$ unpaired electrons.

$\text{Cr}^{3+}$ (Atomic number $24$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^3 \Rightarrow 3$ unpaired electrons.

$\text{Mn}^{3+}$ (Atomic number $25$): $[\text{Ar}] 3d^4 \Rightarrow 4$ unpaired electrons.

Thus, $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ has $5$ unpaired electrons and corresponds to a magnetic moment of $5.92 \text{ BM}$.

Answer: $\text{Mn}^{2+}$

117785.subject: Chemistry
117785.text: What are the coordination number and oxidation state of the central metal ion in the complex $[\text{Fe(EDTA)}]^{-}$?
117785.sol:
The ligand EDTA$^{4-}$ (ethylenediaminetetraacetate) is a hexadentate ligand, meaning it forms six coordinate bonds with the central metal ion. Therefore, the coordination number of iron (Fe) in $[\text{Fe(EDTA)}]^{-}$ is 6.

Let the oxidation state of Fe be $x$. The charge on the EDTA ligand is $-4$.
The sum of the oxidation states must equal the net charge of the complex ion:
$x + (-4) = -1$
$x = +3$

Thus, the coordination number is 6 and the oxidation state is +3.

Answer: 6 and +3

118242.subject: Chemistry
118242.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the reaction of an alkyl halide ($\text{R}-\text{X}$) with different reagents.

List-I (Reagent)List-II (Major Product)
(A) $\text{KCN}$(I) Alkyl isocyanide
(B) $\text{AgCN}$(II) Alkyl cyanide
(C) $\text{KNO}_2$(III) Nitroalkane
(D) $\text{AgNO}_2$(IV) Alkyl nitrite

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
118242.sol:
Cyanide and nitrite ions are ambident nucleophiles.

$\text{KCN}$ is predominantly ionic and provides cyanide ions in solution. Although both carbon and nitrogen atoms are in a position to donate electron pairs, the attack takes place mainly through the carbon atom to form alkyl cyanides (A-II).

$\text{AgCN}$ is mainly covalent in nature and nitrogen is free to donate an electron pair, forming alkyl isocyanides as the major product (B-I).

Similarly, $\text{KNO}_2$ is an ionic compound and the attack occurs through oxygen, resulting in alkyl nitrites (C-IV).

$\text{AgNO}_2$ is covalent and the attack occurs through the nitrogen atom, yielding nitroalkanes as the major product (D-III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

123436.subject: Botany
123436.text:
A student observes the transverse section of a leaf under a microscope and notes the following features:
(a) The mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma.
(b) The upper epidermis possesses some large, empty, and colourless cells along the veins.

Identify the likely group of plants to which this leaf belongs, and the primary function of the specialised cells mentioned in feature (b).
options: Monocotyledonous plant; minimising water loss by leaf curling
Dicotyledonous plant; providing large spaces for storage of sugars
Dicotyledonous plant; minimising water loss by leaf curling
123436.sol:
The presence of an undifferentiated mesophyll (no distinct palisade and spongy parenchyma) is a characteristic feature of an isobilateral leaf, which is typically found in monocotyledonous plants.

The large, empty, and colourless cells on the upper (adaxial) epidermis are bulliform cells. In grasses (monocots), these cells help in minimising water loss during water stress by becoming flaccid, which causes the leaves to curl inwards.

Therefore, the leaf belongs to a monocotyledonous plant, and the specialised cells function to minimise water loss by leaf curling. Bundle sheath cells, not bulliform cells, are involved in C4 photosynthesis.

Answer: Monocotyledonous plant; minimising water loss by leaf curling

123482.text:
Assertion : In angiosperms the conduction of water is more efficient because their xylem has vessels.
Reason : Conduction of water by vessel elements is an active process with energy supplied by xylem parenchyma rich in mitochondria.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
123482.sol: Xylem is the main conducting tissue in plants. It consists of 4 different components - tracheids, trachea or vessels, xylem fibre and xylem parenchyma. Tracheids are elongated cells with tapering end. They are generally present in ferns and gymnosperms for conduction of water. In angiosperms, vessels are composite structure as these are formed by dissolution of end walls of row of cells i.e., vessels elements. So angiosperms, have more efficient system of conduction due to presence of vessels. Conduction of water by vessel elements is also known as ascent of sap. Water absorbed by roots, goes upward to replace the water loss by transpiration. The most accepted theory for ascent of sap is transpiration pull theory i.e., when water is lost by transpiration from the leaves, a tension is created in the xylem and due to this water absorbed by roots hair is passed through vessels to the leaves. The xylem parenchyma are mainly for storage function but sometimes help in conduction.

Plasmalemma, a trilaminar and selectively permeable membrane covering the body, functions both in excretion (ammonia) and respiration in Amoeba.Pseudopodia (false feet) are finger-like and blunt-extensions of cell body in protozoans. In Amoeba, the type of pseudopodium found in lobopodium, composed of both ectoplasm and endoplasm. It is temporary locomotory structure which is also meant for feeding in Amoeba. Locomotion of Amoeba is known as'amoeboid movement' (Sol-gel theory).

124927.sol: The complete combustion of glucose, which produces CO2 and H2O as end products, yields energy most of which is given out as heat. The strategy that the plant cell uses is to catabolize the glucose molecule in such a way that not all the liberated energy goes out as heat.

125340.subject: Botany
125340.text: How many pigments contribute to the color seen in leaves?
125340.sol: Looking at plants have you ever wondered why and how there are so many shades of green in their leaves – even in the same plant? We can look for an answer to this question by trying to separate the leaf pigments of any green plant through paper chromatography. A chromatographic separation of the leaf pigments shows that the colour that we see in leaves is not due to a single pigment but due to four pigments: Chlorophyll a (bright or blue green in the chromatogram), chlorophyll b (yellow green), xanthophylls (yellow) and carotenoids (yellow to yellow-orange). Let us now see what roles various pigments play in photosynthesis.
125340.meta: How many pigments contribute to the color seen in leaves?

125366.subject: Botany
125366.text: How is the movement of electrons described in the electron transport chain?
125366.sol: In photosystem II the reaction centre chlorophyll a absorbs 680 nm wavelength of red light causing electrons to become excited and jump into an orbit farther from the atomic nucleus. These electrons are picked up by an electron acceptor which passes them to an electrons transport system consisting of cytochromes. This movement of electrons is downhill, in terms of an oxidation-reduction or redox potential scale. The electrons are not used up as they pass through the electron transport chain, but are passed on to the pigments of photosystem PS I. Simultaneously, electrons in the reaction centre of PS I are also excited when they receive red light of wavelength 700 nm and are transferred to another accepter molecule that has a greater redox potential.
125366.meta: How is the movement of electrons described in the electron transport chain?

125780.subject: Botany
125780.text: Where is the proximal end of the filament attached?
125780.sol: the two parts of a typical stamen – the long and slender stalk called the filament, and the terminal generally bilobed structure called the anther. The proximal end of the filament is attached to the thalamus or the petal of the flower. The number and length of stamens are variable in flowers of different species. If you were to collect a stamen each from ten flowers (each from different species) and arrange them on a slide, you would be able to appreciate the large variation in size seen in nature. Careful observation of each stamen under a dissecting microscope and making neat diagrams would elucidate the range in shape and attachment of anthers in different flowers. A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed with each lobe having two theca, i.e., they are dithecous Often a longitudinal groove runs lengthwise separating the theca.
125780.meta: Where is the proximal end of the filament attached?

125918.subject: Botany
125918.text: What does pollination not guarantee according to the paragraph?
options: The growth of the pollen tube
The entry of pollen into the ovule
125918.sol: Pollination does not guarantee the transfer of the right type of pollen (compatible pollen of the same species as the stigma). Often, pollen of the wrong type, either from other species or from the same plant (if it is self-incompatible), also land on the stigma. The pistil has the ability to recognise the pollen, whether it is of the right type(compatible) or of the wrong type (incompatible). If it is of the right type, the pistil accepts the pollen and promotes post-pollination events that leads to fertilisation. If the pollen is of the wrong type, the pistil rejects the pollen by preventing pollen germination on the stigma or the pollen tube growth in the style. The ability of the pistil to recognise the pollen followed by its acceptance or rejection is the result of a continuous dialogue between pollen grain and the pistil.

126292.subject: Botany
126292.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
A. Antipodal cellI. $n+n$
B. Central cell (prior to fertilization)II. $3n$
C. ZygoteIII. $n$
D. Primary endosperm cellIV. $2n$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
126292.sol:
Antipodal cells are part of the female gametophyte and are haploid ($n$).

The central cell, before fertilization, contains two polar nuclei and its genetic constitution is represented as $n+n$.

The zygote is formed by syngamy (fusion of a male gamete with the egg cell) and is diploid ($2n$).

The primary endosperm cell is formed by triple fusion (fusion of a male gamete with two polar nuclei) and is triploid ($3n$).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
